title: Regenerate produces a new draft server-side but the visible textarea never updates
problem: Clicking Regenerate flashes "Regenerating…" then shows the OLD draft — the textarea is seeded once from useState and DraftRail is keyed only on ticket.id (unchanged on regenerate), so it never re-syncs; the rep may re-send stale text believing it is new.
evidence: tideover/components/product/DraftRail.tsx:56 (`useState(...)` no effect on draftText); tideover/app/app/inbox/page.tsx:255 (`<DraftRail key={view.ticket.id}>`); tideover/components/product/ApprovalBar.tsx:85-96 (regenerate() posts then only router.refresh()); tideover/app/api/draft/route.ts:15 returns fresh draft the caller discards.
proposal: Thread the regenerate result into the editor: add an onRegenerated(newText) callback from DraftRail to ApprovalBar, read data.draft.text and setText (reset mode to standard), or include a regen nonce in DraftRail's key so it remounts; guard against clobbering unsaved edits and show a "New draft ready" cue.

verdict.note: Verified against source: DraftRail.tsx:56 seeds `text` via useState only, no effect syncing to draftText prop; page.tsx:255 keys DraftRail on `view.ticket.id` alone (unchanged by regenerate); ApprovalBar.tsx:85-96 regenerate() posts to /api/draft and discards the response, calling only router.refresh(); api/draft/route.ts:15 confirms the endpoint returns the fresh draft.text that is never read. Net effect: after a server refresh the new draftText prop arrives but React does not reinitialize existing component state for an unchanged key, so the textarea keeps showing stale text while UI implies a fresh regen — a rep (esp. untrained persona A on an escalated ticket) can approve-and-send stale content believing it's new. Proposal (thread callback or bump key/nonce on regenerate) is low-risk, doesn't touch approve/send posting path or ⌘/Ctrl+Enter (which reads live `text` state via getText()), and adds no fabricated copy — proof-only doctrine unaffected. P1 is justified given escalation-grade blast radius and zero existing mitigation.

title: Escalated/hostile flag in the queue is a near-invisible unlabeled 6px dot
problem: The most operationally important triage signal — this customer is hostile or threatening a chargeback — is a 6px dot with no label, independent of the risk-score pill (a ticket can show a calm amber/green risk pill while escalated), so a rep scanning by risk color can walk right past a chargeback threat.
evidence: tideover/components/product/QueueList.tsx:72-77 (`aria-label="escalated"` on a bare 6px bg-risk-red span, no visible text/title, unlike SlaChip's title at tideover/components/product/SlaChip.tsx:24); tideover/app/app/inbox/page.tsx:41-43 (escalatedSentiment() is a separate signal from riskScore/color).
proposal: Replace the bare dot with a small visible text pill (e.g. `pill pill-red` "Escalated") next to the risk badge in QueueList so hostile/chargeback tickets read at a glance without opening them; keep the dot only as decoration.

verdict.note: Verified at QueueList.tsx:72-77 — escalated flag is literally `h-1.5 w-1.5` (6px) bg-risk-red dot with only an aria-label (screen-reader only, no visible text/title), while SlaChip.tsx:24 uses a visible `title` tooltip and adjacent risk-score pill is the only visible-text signal on the row. inbox/page.tsx:41-43 confirms escalatedSentiment (hostile/chargeback-threat) is computed independently from riskScore/color, so the finding's core claim (calm-colored pill + escalation can co-occur, and the flag is easy to miss scanning by color) holds and is not solved elsewhere in the tree. Proposal (small visible red pill next to risk badge) is low-effort, doesn't touch approve/send flow or keyboard shortcuts (QueueKeyboard untouched), and adds only a static label — no fabricated metrics/dates, no proof-only violation. Given persona A (untrained rep triaging escalations) this is a real miss-a-chargeback-threat risk, so P1 is justified.

title: No confirmation that a normal Approve & send worked before the view jumps to the next ticket
problem: On the common send path the UI instantly router.replace()s to a different customer with a different draft — no toast, no "Reply sent" — so a day-one rep who just replied to a hostile customer can't tell it worked, panics, and may re-click or ask a human.
evidence: tideover/components/product/ApprovalBar.tsx:108-131 (approveSend success calls advance() with zero confirmation), :124 (advance fires immediately), vs :152-163 (the "Reply sent." card renders only for already-sent/sentMeta tickets); no aria-live/role="status" in the file.
proposal: Before advance(), briefly render the existing "Reply sent." confirmation (hold ~300-700ms or until keypress) wrapped in role="status" aria-live="polite" so sighted and screen-reader operators both perceive success; optionally make auto-advance opt-in or label it.

verdict.note: Verified against tideover/components/product/ApprovalBar.tsx: approveSend() (98-132) calls advance() unconditionally at line 124 on the normal send path, which immediately router.replace()s to the next ticket with zero rendered feedback. The "Reply sent." card (152-163) is gated behind `sentMeta`, which is only ever set from `alreadySent` at mount (line 48-50) for deep-linked already-sent tickets — the live-send path never sets it, so it can't and doesn't fire on a fresh approve. Repo-wide grep for aria-live/role="status"/toast turns up nothing related to send confirmation anywhere else in the tree, so there's no other component quietly covering this. The proposal (hold the existing "Reply sent." UI briefly or until keypress, wrapped in role="status" aria-live="polite") is feasible: busy state already stays true through the navigation per the code comment, so gating advance() behind a short timeout/keypress is a local, non-breaking change that doesn't touch the hard-date gate, promote flow, or fabricate any metric — it just reuses existing sent copy. It also doesn't conflict with the ⌘/Ctrl+Enter shortcut since the proposal explicitly allows keypress-to-skip for the power-user persona (B). Severity is justified for persona A (untrained rep on a hostile ticket) since silent success plausibly causes real-world duplicate outreach/panic, not just cosmetic annoyance.

title: "Escalate" button is cosmetic: nothing is persisted, no manager is notified

evidence: tideover/components/product/ApprovalBar.tsx:45 (local useState), :216-220 ("Flagged for manager review this window."), :233-239 (onClick toggles local state, no fetch/post); tideover/app/app/inbox/page.tsx:78 (queue's own escalated flag derived from ticket.sentiment, unrelated); repo-wide grep of app/api and lib for "escalat" returns zero routes/fields.
proposal: Wire Escalate to a persisted POST /api/escalate that writes an `escalated-by:<operator>`+timestamp tag (reuse the gift-sent tag pattern) and surface flagged tickets in the queue/dashboard; until built, remove copy implying a manager was notified (relabel e.g. "Mark for my own follow-up") and persist the flag so it survives navigation.

title: Lead the dashboard with the daily action instead of two analytics panels
problem: Landing on /app the founder scrolls past six baseline tiles, a big "money at risk" panel, and a risk-curve chart before reaching the At-risk queue and the only "Open cockpit" link — the thing they came to act on — and the biggest, boldest number on the page is an anxiety estimate with no next step attached.

title: ink-mute fails WCAG AA contrast and carries most of the cockpit's secondary + QA copy
problem: --ink-mute (#6A7B80) computes to ~4.16:1 on --sand and ~4.41:1 on --paper — both below the 4.5:1 AA minimum for normal text — yet it colors the bulk of small supporting copy including the QA-checklist hint that tells a rep exactly what to fix before a blocked send.
evidence: tideover/app/globals.css:10-11 (--sand:#fbf8f2), :26 (--ink-mute:#6a7b80), tideover/tailwind.config.ts:35; used at tideover/components/product/DraftRail.tsx:227 (QA hint) and tideover/app/app/inbox/page.tsx:286-293 (DetailStat label); ~76 uses of text-ink-mute across the 11 page files.

verdict.note: Verified the contrast math independently: --ink-mute #6A7B80 vs --sand #fbf8f2 computes to ~4.16:1 and vs --paper #ffffff to ~4.41:1, both below the 4.5:1 AA threshold for normal text — matches the finding exactly. Confirmed usage sites: DraftRail.tsx:227 QA-hint text is 11.5px and inbox/page.tsx:289 DetailStat label is 11px — both well under the 18px/14px-bold large-text exemption, so full AA applies and both fail. Grep shows 164 uses across 45 files (auditor undercounted at ~76 but direction is right) with no alternate higher-contrast token already covering these hint/label spots — not solved elsewhere. Proposal (darken the single CSS/tailwind token) is feasible, doesn't touch approve/send logic or shortcuts, and introduces no fabricated copy — proof-only doctrine is untouched. P2 is right: real accessibility defect hitting the exact QA-checklist hint text both personas rely on under pressure, but text remains legible to most users so it's not flow-blocking like a P1.

title: Customer-facing "Order" tag leaks the raw internal database ID

I downgrade severity from P1 to P2: the page's branded header, first-name greeting, and merchant name give strong legitimacy signals already: an odd-looking order-id tag is a minor trust wrinkle, not a plausible "phishing" trigger, and doesn't block either persona (junior CS rep or solo founder) from doing their job. The copy-reframe half of the proposal ("account owner still needs to finish setup, you can start answering tickets now") is cheap and feasible, touches no hot files, adds no fabricated metrics/dates, and doesn't affect approve/send or keyboard shortcuts, so the finding survives with a real, low-cost fix path even though the role-gating half is underscoped on effort. P2 is right — confusing/wasteful for an untrained rep but not blocking, and she'd likely just navigate back to Inbox rather than being truly stuck.

title: Keyboard send loop breaks after every auto-advance — the new draft isn't re-focused, so ⌘↵ silently does nothing
problem: The header promises "⌘↵ to send," but ⌘↵ only fires inside the focused draft textarea; after a send auto-advances to the next ticket the new textarea is NOT focused, so pressing ⌘↵ again does nothing and the rep must press Enter to re-focus before every single send — breaking the rhythm the hint advertises.
evidence: hint at tideover/app/app/inbox/page.tsx:144-146; tideover/components/product/QueueKeyboard.tsx:73 (`if (e.metaKey||e.ctrlKey||e.altKey) return` ignores ⌘↵ from queue focus); ⌘↵ handled only inside the textarea DraftRail.tsx:160-166; advance() ApprovalBar.tsx:77-83 navigates but never refocuses; focus only on Enter via focusDraftEditor QueueKeyboard.tsx:124-135.
proposal: After a successful send/advance, auto-focus the newly mounted draft textarea (a DraftRail mount effect, or call focusDraftEditor for the advanced ticket) so ⌘↵ works cycle-to-cycle; or reword the hint to "Enter to open, then ⌘↵ to send" so the extra step is honest.

verdict.note: Verified at cited lines: QueueKeyboard.tsx:73 bails on any modifier combo (by design, so ⌘/Ctrl+Enter falls through to native textarea handling); DraftRail.tsx:160-166 binds ⌘/Ctrl+Enter only on the focused textarea; ApprovalBar.tsx:77-83 advance() is a bare router.replace with no focus call; grepped DraftRail.tsx for autoFocus/.focus() — none exists, so the newly mounted textarea after auto-advance is genuinely unfocused. Header hint (page.tsx:144-146) literally reads "⌘↵ to send" with no caveat, so the claim is accurate, not mischaracterized. Not a safety issue (nothing silently sends wrong content; the rep just sees no advance and re-presses Enter), but it does break the promised rhythm every single cycle for persona B's 15-min/day workflow. Fix is feasible and low-risk: either call focusDraftEditor-equivalent logic in a DraftRail mount effect keyed on ticketId, or soften the hint copy — neither touches proof-only doctrine, SAMPLE DATA watermarking, or the approve/send path itself. P2 is right: real, cheap to fix, but not escalation-grade/blocking.

title: Keyboard-shortcut send hint shows only the Mac ⌘ glyph, no Ctrl equivalent

verdict.note: Verified: inbox/page.tsx:145 shows only "⌘↵ to send" and DraftRail.tsx:163 confirms Ctrl+Enter is fully functional but never surfaced anywhere in user-visible text (only in code comments). Severity P3 is right: it's a discoverability gap, not a broken flow — Ctrl+Enter still works, reps can fall back to mouse-click send, and this only affects first-day onboarding friction for Windows users (persona A most affected).

title: Keyboard shortcuts are poorly discoverable — one 11px muted caption, only on the Inbox when the queue is non-empty

tideover/app/app/inbox/page.tsx:143-147 (`

J/K to move · Enter to open · ⌘↵ to send

`, only when items.length>0); tideover/components/product/QueueKeyboard.tsx implements the full handler with no other discovery surface.

title: "Save this edit as a variant" prompt uses undefined jargon and blocks the send flow
problem: After a >30% edit the rep is stopped by "Save it as a tracked variant so it competes in the panel?" — "tracked variant" and "the panel" are unexplained at the moment of decision, it never says what happens to the edit on "Not now," and the whole ask blocks what should just be "sent, next."

title: Hover-only tooltips have no visual affordance, so reps never discover them (and they don't fire on touch)
problem: Good explainers exist (FactorBreakdown labels, SlaChip's chip, Customers links) but they're plain text with a native title and zero visual cue — no dotted underline, no (?) glyph — so a first-day rep has no reason to hover, and native title tooltips don't fire on touch at all.

title: No "already set up? Sign in" affordance on the onboarding page
problem: The onboarding wizard offers no path back to /login, so a returning founder whose session expired and who navigates to /onboarding from memory/bookmark/stale link gets no signal they may already have an account and could re-run the full wizard, generating a second merchant/playbook.
